learning_objective: 🎯 Learn how to add exciting details to your actions using adverbs, and master exactly where to place them in a sentence!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Adverbs are words that upgrade or describe Verbs, Adjectives, or even other Adverbs! They answer the important questions: How? When? Where? and How often? Example: 'She runs QUICKLY.' (Quickly tells us HOW she runs).

These tell us HOW an action is done. They usually end in '-ly' (like loudly, quietly, happily). POSITION RULE: Put them right AFTER the main verb or after the object. Example: 'He played the guitar BEAUTIFULLY.'

main_concepts.concept_title: ⏰📍 Adverbs of Time & Place (When and Where)
main_concepts.simple_explanation: Time adverbs answer 'When?' (today, tomorrow, soon). Place adverbs answer 'Where?' (here, there, everywhere). POSITION RULE: We usually place these at the very END of a sentence. Example: 'We are going to the park TOMORROW.'

These tell us how often something happens (always, never, sometimes, usually). POSITION RULE: These are tricky! Place them BEFORE the main verb, but AFTER helping verbs like 'is, am, are'. Example: 'I ALWAYS brush my teeth' but 'I am ALWAYS happy.'

What if you have three adverbs in one sentence? Use the MPT rule! Manner first, then Place, then Time. Example: 'She sang beautifully (Manner) at the concert (Place) last night (Time).' Do not mix the order!

fun_activity.title: 🕵️‍♂️ The MPT Sentence Builder
fun_activity.instructions: Take the basic sentence 'The dog barked.' Now, add an adverb of Manner, Place, and Time using the MPT rule! (Hint: How did it bark? Where? When?) Example: The dog barked loudly outside yesterday.

quick_recap: ⭐ Adverbs describe verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs.
⭐ Place (Where?) and Time (When?) usually go at the end of the sentence.
⭐ Frequency (How often?) goes before the main verb.
⭐ Remember the MPT rule for multiple adverbs: Manner, then Place, then Time.
